title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval - Meridian Biotech
next_steps: Redwood to share updated benchmark spreadsheet with quantized model A/B results
Customer to provide additional 200 prompt samples for rare-case regression checks
Schedule technical deep dive on dedicated deployment options w/ infra team 2026-05-20
action_items: Alex Chen: Send pricing deck and pilot SOW by 2026-05-15
Samira Patel: Upload latest eval scripts and scoring rubric link to shared drive by 2026-05-14
Tom Huang: Run internal privacy check and confirm data residency requirements by 2026-05-18
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on quality regressions seen after model update; reviewed prompt set scoring, guardrails and next actions to run A/B with quantized variant and validate security controls for Private/Dedicated options.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, this is the week three POC sync for Meridian Biotech. We are at about 45 minutes, is that right, Samira?
[00:08] Samira Patel: Yeah looks like 45, should be enough to hit the highlights.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Thanks Alex. Quick note, we did a small pre-run of the new prompt set against the dev model this morning and flagged a few unexpected outputs.
[00:22] Samira Patel: Right, so we pulled the logs and the scoring - uh we saw a regression on the clinical-note normalization tasks, about a 6% drop in F1 on the high-precision set.
[00:33] Tom Huang: I saw that too, there were some hallucinated drug dosages on a couple of samples, which is worrisome.
[00:40] Alex Chen: Okay let's unpack that. First, can you describe which prompt templates triggered the issues? Was this an input distribution shift or a model-side change?
[00:50] Priya Nair: Mostly the templated SOAP note inputs — the ones where the patient note contains shorthand and nested lists. The new model seemed to over-expand abbreviations incorrectly e.g., 'ASA' turned into multiple things.
[01:02] Samira Patel: Just to clarify, we rolled a minor model variant update last week to the hosted stack — it's the rwd-v1.4-optim drop-in. Some of the kernel selection heuristics changed and that changed tokenization slightly, so rare tokens got different encodings. That can explain abbreviation expansion differences.
[01:18] Evan Brooks: Is rwd-v1.4-optim the Redwood model name? I thought we were on rwd-v1.3?
[01:24] Samira Patel: Sorry, yeah I meant v1.3.4 patched with new compilation settings — the name gets a little fuzzy on calls sometimes.
[01:29] Lena Ortiz: From a security standpoint, before we discuss mitigation, can you confirm whether the trial data processed on hosted endpoints is stored? We need assurance for the compliance team — SOC 2, encryption at rest and KMS usage.
[01:42] Alex Chen: Short answer: for the hosted POC we have data retention controls; by default logs are ephemeral for the trial but we can turn on strict retention policies for the pilot. All data at rest is encrypted and we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments. We'll follow up with the security docs.
[01:56] Samira Patel: Also to add, the Private deployment option gives you full control over keys and VPC isolation, if you need air-gapped like setups or on-prem.
[02:05] Tom Huang: Good. Back to the regression — what are the immediate mitigation steps?
[02:09] Samira Patel: We have a couple paths: 1) revert the compilation change on the hosted instance to the previous kernel selection, 2) apply prompt-level guardrails / post-processing to normalize shorthand, 3) run an A/B with a quantized model that preserves previous tokenization.
[02:24] Priya Nair: The post-processing might be fastest. We have an internal regex-based normalizer that we could apply before scoring. But it only covers common abbreviations, not all edge cases.
[02:34] Samira Patel: Right, and our scoring harness can be configured to run both pre- and post-normalization so you can see delta. We'll push the updated scoring scripts to the shared drive.
[02:44] Alex Chen: Can we get numbers? Samira, can you summarize the current metrics and what changed?
[02:48] Samira Patel: Sure, quick numbers: baseline F1 on the high-precision set was 0.87 with v1.3; after the patch it's 0.82 on the same set. Precision dropped more than recall, suggesting false positives / over-expansions. The aggregate token latency stayed within SLO for hosted — median 140ms per request, 95th at 420ms. Cost per 1k tokens increased by about 7% due to the compile path change.
[03:12] Evan Brooks: 7% is ok but the clinical hallucination is the blocker.
[03:16] Samira Patel: Agreed. For the A/B we can spin up a quantized variant on a dedicated pool or on hosted with a pinned model. Quantization tends to change the numeric kernels but can preserve tokenization; results vary.
[03:29] Tom Huang: We prefer dedicated for latency predictability and for the compliance team. What's the capacity lead time?
[03:33] Alex Chen: For a short pilot we can reserve a small dedicated instance within 24-48 hours if there's capacity. For larger throughput we may need a short lead time. We'll share Dedicated pricing in the deck.
[03:44] Lena Ortiz: Also, for Dedicated or Private we need RBAC controls, audit logs, and SAML SSO. Do you support those?
[03:51] Samira Patel: Yes — RBAC is configurable in the Console, audit logs are available and we support SAML/SO for SSO, and integrate with enterprise IdPs. I'll attach the security checklist.
[04:02] Priya Nair: On scoring and prompts: we ran the new 500-sample prompt set, and the guardrail filters caught some PII leakage but missed shorthand mis-expansions. We need guardrail rules specifically for clinical abbreviations.
[04:16] Samira Patel: Our guardrails engine is rule-based plus model-based checks. We can add custom regex rules for the abbreviations and run them as a pre-filter. We should be careful not to overfilter and drop valid expansions.
[04:28] Evan Brooks: Could that cause recall issues?
[04:30] Samira Patel: Potentially, yes. That's why we run parallel scoring and show you the delta with/without rules in the dashboard.
[04:36] Alex Chen: Let's propose a hybrid: apply prompt-level normalization for the top 50 abbreviations, run A/B with the quantized model, and revert the compilation change on the hosted instance if the A/B fails. Sound ok?
[04:48] Priya Nair: Yes that sounds pragmatic.
[04:50] Tom Huang: For the A/B, can we include the rare-case prompt set (200 samples) that we mentioned? We want those in the test harness.
[04:56] Samira Patel: Absolutely — please upload those samples to the shared folder and we'll include them.
[05:02] Alex Chen: Samira, you'll own the A/B run and share the spreadsheet, Samira confirms?
[05:06] Samira Patel: Yep I'll run the A/B and post the results. Expect the first pass by Friday.
[05:12] Lena Ortiz: Also, please share SOC2 cert and encryption at rest docs; we need to check with infosec.
[05:18] Alex Chen: Will do. We'll attach the security bundle and the KMS integration notes.
[05:22] Evan Brooks: Any risk if we switch to Dedicated for A/B? Will the results be comparable to hosted?
[05:27] Samira Patel: There can be minor differences due to kernel selection and hardware (GPU type), but we try to keep model binaries consistent. We'll document any drift. For strict comparability, we can run both on same underlying model binary but on different infra — that reduces infra-caused variance.
[05:42] Tom Huang: Ok that helps. One more question on logging — can we redact or obfuscate PHI in logs automatically?
[05:48] Samira Patel: We have a configurable PII redaction pipeline and you can enable client-side redaction too. For sensitive pilots we recommend both.
[05:55] Priya Nair: Good. Curious about timeline and deliverables.
[05:58] Alex Chen: Timeline: Samira to run A/B and share by 2026-05-15; Alex to send pricing + SOW by 2026-05-15; Meridian to upload 200 rare-case samples by 2026-05-14; Tech deep dive scheduled for 2026-05-20. We'll reconvene next week same time to review results.
[06:15] Evan Brooks: That works. Anything else on guardrails?
[06:18] Samira Patel: I'll include suggested regex rules and show tradeoffs in the scoring report.
[06:23] Alex Chen: Great. Quick recap of open action items and owners: (brief pause) Samira?
[06:28] Samira Patel: Upload eval scripts and scoring rubric to shared drive; run A/B with quantized variant and produce spreadsheet; include delta for rare-case set.
[06:39] Alex Chen: I'll share pricing and SOW and the security artifacts. Meridian team to upload rare-case prompts and run internal privacy check.
[06:47] Priya Nair: We'll do that. Appreciate the speed.
[06:50] Lena Ortiz: One last ask: can you include a short doc on how model rollbacks are handled in Redwood Console for audit? Our auditors will ask.
[06:59] Samira Patel: Yes I'll add a rollback/runbook snippet to the security bundle.
[07:05] Alex Chen: Ok thanks everyone. We'll email the notes and actions. Meeting adjourned.
[07:10] (call ends)
